description: Child-safe housing for the busy board PCB: a front plate carrying the buttons, pots, encoder and switches, a black printed frame, a back tray for the board and battery pack, and a screwed battery door. It fits two board versions. v3.0 (the default, 235.6 x 247.6 mm outside) is seen through a 3 mm clear polycarbonate plate that is cut from a DXF, not printed. v2.0 (board_v3 off, 247.6 mm square outside) has an opaque printed plate that every LED glows through. The printing notes say which files each version needs.

hardware.item: Busy board PCB v3.0, 210 x 222 mm (factory assembled by JLCPCB), or v2.0 with board_v3 off
hardware.notes: St-John-Software/electronics, hardware/busy-board-v3/ (v3.0, the default) or hardware/busy-board/ (v2.0, 222 mm square); dimensions from docs/busy-board-v3/PCB.md and docs/busy-board/PCB.md

hardware.item: 3 mm clear polycarbonate sheet, cut to busy_board_plate.dxf (v3 only)
hardware.notes: v3 only: v2 prints its plate (busy_board_plate_v2.stl). 213.4 x 225.4 mm, R3 corners; polycarbonate, not acrylic (acrylic cracks and shatters). Routed and drilled by a UK cut-to-size service (no laser: it yellows and stresses PC), holes down to 1.5 mm; protective film both sides. DXF: https://www.bstjohn.net/3d-models/busy_board_plate.dxf

hardware.item: 3 mm clear polycarbonate pane, 58 x 25 mm (v2 DS1 window)
hardware.notes: v2 only: sawn from a small offcut, deburred; drops into the printed plate's pocket from behind over the 48 x 17 mm display opening and is clamped by busy_board_window_retainer.stl (ds1_pane, ds1_pane_t)
v3: four play buttons and the power button; v2: five play buttons; held by its own panel nut, no push-on cap
v2 only (board_v3 off): Switch Electronics 490321, Off-(On) SPST-NO, 19 mm cut-out (pwr_hole_d), 2.8 mm spade terminals; momentary only, a latching switch would hold the power latch on

hardware.item: 10k linear panel pot, 17 mm RK163 with anti-rotation tab
hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 133042 (mono, solder lugs) or in-stock fallback 133085 (RK163G stereo, PCB pins, one gang wired); M7 x 0.75 bushing, 7 mm cut-out (pot_hole_d)

hardware.item: 20 mm rotary encoder with push switch, panel-mount (bushing and nut)
hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 482026 (MPN 483363), 24 detents, M7 x 0.5 bushing, 7 mm cut-out (enc_hole_d)
Switch Electronics 486015; 1/4-40 UNS bushing, 6.5 mm cut-out (tgl_hole_d); fixed metal lever, no sealing boot or lever cap
Switch Electronics 490906 (MOQ 10); its tab goes through the plate's tab hole (tgl_lug_r, tgl_lug_d)

hardware.item: On-On slide switch with two screw ears
hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 124002 (MOQ 10); ears 19 mm apart (slide_screw_pitch); actuator part of the switch

hardware.item: CLIFF K15 knob, set-screw fixing, 20 mm
hardware.notes: Switch Electronics 484151 (MPN CL172962); on the pots and the encoder; no push-on knobs

hardware.item: 14500 (AA-format) cell holder with leads, no clip-on cover
hardware.notes: Side by side in the compartment, wired in parallel
1S3P pack, matched within 50 mV before paralleling; never user-removable
Between the cells and J1, on foam tape in the tray's PCM pocket
In the cradle behind the left-wall plug pocket, component side down

hardware.item: M3 heat-set insert (4.6 mm OD, up to 6 mm long)
hardware.notes: Eight frame posts, eight tray PCB posts, one door boss and (v2) four DS1 retainer bosses on the printed plate; set insert_hole_d to 2.6 for self-tapping screws instead

hardware.item: M3 x 15 M-F nylon hex standoff (6 mm male thread)
hardware.notes: Through board holes H1-H8 into the tray's PCB posts; their tops press the plate into the frame lip and set the board 15 mm behind it (standoff_l == pcb_to_panel)
Through the tray floor into the panel posts
Battery door
v2 only: the DS1 window retainer into the inserts in the printed plate's bosses (ret_screw_l)
Slide switch: from the play side through the plate (v3: and a spacer) and the switch's ears
v3 only: between the clear plate and each slide-switch ear (slide_spacer_h); v2's ears screw straight to the 5 mm printed slab
Behind each slide-switch ear, so the screws cannot work loose

printing_notes: Which files: v3 board (the default) - print busy_board_frame, busy_board_tray and busy_board_battery_door, and have the plate cut from busy_board_plate.dxf (busy_board_plate.stl is for viewing only). v2 board - print busy_board_plate_v2 and busy_board_window_retainer, the frame and tray re-rendered with board_v3 off in the customizer, and the same door. busy_board_plate_v2_coupon is a small test piece cut from the v2 plate: print it first to check fits and LED glow.

Print the frame, tray and door in matte black PETG or ASA, 3 perimeters, without supports: the frame play face down with a brim, the tray floor down, the door outer face down. Frame and tray are 235.6 x 247.6 mm (v2: 247.6 mm square) and need a 250 mm bed (A1). v3's clear plate is not printed: its STL is for viewing only.

v3: have the 3 mm clear polycarbonate plate (not acrylic) routed and drilled from https://www.bstjohn.net/3d-models/busy_board_plate.dxf, which the build exports from the OpenSCAD model and draws as seen from the play side. Its only openings are the control, tab, slide-switch and grille holes; keep the protective film on until assembly.

v2 printed plate (busy_board_plate_v2.stl): white or another light PETG (ASA as the alternative, never PLA; black passes no light), play face down, 0.2 mm layers, 4 walls, 5 top and bottom layers, 40 % gyroid infill, brim, no supports. Print busy_board_plate_v2_coupon.stl first in the same filament and settings: check a toggle and a pot in their seats, and that the LED and bar windows glow evenly, before the full plate.

v2 display window: press four M3 inserts into the plate's retainer bosses, drop the 58 x 25 mm clear pane into its pocket from behind, then screw busy_board_window_retainer.stl (printed plate down, in any colour) over it with four M3 x 6 pan-head screws. The pane is larger than its opening, so nothing can be pushed out from the play side.

v2 weak points: layers lie in the plate plane, so each 24.5 mm button hole is ringed by continuous perimeters, with ribs running through the 13.5 mm webs between holes; the toggle locking-ring tabs bear on the walls of blind keyways, not on a thin web; LED skins span at most 6 mm (bar cells 4.4 mm) and are closed, though a sharp tool could pierce one.
The v2 rib grid that carries a push to the eight perimeter standoffs is a judgement, not an engineer's check: press hard on the printed plate on the bench before it goes to the child.
Press the M3 heat-set inserts before assembly: eight in the frame posts, eight in the tray's PCB posts, one in the door boss and, on v2, four in the printed plate's DS1 retainer bosses (21 in all).

Assembly order: screw the eight M3 x 15 standoffs through H1-H8 into the tray's PCB posts, which seats the board; fit the buttons, pots, encoder and toggles to the plate with their panel nuts (tabs in their holes or keyways), the slide switch with two M2 x 10 screws and nylocs (v3: with 2 mm spacers; v2: straight onto the printed slab, no spacers), then the set-screw knobs; drop the plate into the frame's rebate; plug each control lead into the connector beside its cut-out; close up.
The two slide-switch pan-head screws are the one approved play-side fastener besides the control nuts; their nylocs keep them captive. Every other fixing is behind the plate or under the tray.

Tray, by an adult: hot-glue the CR-TL24 into its cradle component side down, sliding it toward the left wall until its USB-C socket passes the pocket's end wall and its charge LEDs sit over the two floor windows. Stick the PCM into its pocket on foam tape. Parallel the three matched cells in their holders, wire them through the PCM to J1 and the charger, and seat the holders in the compartment from the back with the leads through the -X notch.

Close up: frame onto the tray with eight M3 x 10 countersunk screws from the back, which presses the plate onto the standoffs, then the battery door with its M3 x 8. The door needs a screwdriver (adult-only access, cells are never user-removable); J9 is only reachable with the tray off. Charge from the recessed USB-C pocket in the left wall.

The LEDs sit on the board with no spacers. v3's 5050s are 13.4 mm behind the clear plate and no panel diffuses them; v2's glow through 0.8 mm skins in the printed plate, each in a light tube or baffle cell. Re-check brightness on the bench (BENCH_BRINGUP steps 7.5 and 11.7) before the board goes to the child; a window that is too dim needs a thinner skin (win_skin_t, not below 0.6 mm), not a higher brightness cap.

Toggles: the 3 mm plate (v2: the 3 mm seat pocketed into the printed plate) takes one nut (APEM allows 4 mm with one nut, 2.5 mm with two). Fit each APEM 5636A from behind with the U215 locking ring on its bushing, tab through its plate hole (v2: into its blind keyway), then the switch's lockwasher and one 8 mm A/F nut on the play face.

VERIFY with the parts in hand: the plate sits flat on the standoffs with no rattle; the control leads reach with the plate held over the board; slide_spacer_h and screw size (M2 assumed: slide_screw_l, slide_head_d, slide_nut_d; the build checks nut and screw clearance); tab holes (pot_lug_a, pot_lug_r, pot_lug_d, tgl_lug_r, tgl_lug_d, enc_lug); the cutting service's minimum hole (1.5 mm assumed) and that it accepts 64-sided polylines instead of CIRCLEs.

VERIFY against the delivered parts and adjust: arcade button depth, nut and switch reach (button_depth, button_nut_d, button_switch_reach) and the v2 mushroom power switch (pwr_hole_d, pwr_nut_d, pwr_depth); the toggle face and depth (tgl_face_d, tgl_depth); and the pot and encoder depths (pot_depth, enc_depth).

VERIFY the pack side too: cell holder size (batt_l, batt_w, batt_h); PCM size (pcm_l, pcm_w); the CR-TL24 outline, seat height and LED positions (chg_l, chg_w, chg_seat, chg_led) and its USB-C plug overmould (usb_pocket_d); and the JST-XH lead room (raising pcb_to_panel needs longer standoffs: standoff_l).

VERIFY for v2's printed plate: the pot bushing length (pot_thread_l 6.5 mm, Alpha RV16 datasheet) and encoder bushing length (enc_thread_l 5 mm, the shortest EC11 option), since the seller's pages could not be fetched; the U215 tab height (set tgl_lug_through if it is over 2.4 mm); the TO-92 height (to92_h); and the DS1 pane thickness (ds1_pane_t).

wall, corner_r, edge_r, inner_d, insert_hole_d and lip_clear are shared by the frame and the tray, panel_t by the frame and the plate, and floor_t, batt_l, batt_w, door_t and door_clear by the tray and the door: set them identically on every part that exposes them.
